items.synopsis: Major alarms for fabric link faults that result in reduced fabric capacity are introduced on PTX10004 and PTX10008 platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX10004 and PTX10008 platforms with LC1301 line cards and SF5 fabric, fabric link faults need to be reported as major alarms. Link faults can occur during system operation and result in reduced fabric capacity with partial impact. This enhancement introduces the new alarm "One or more PFE pairs operating with less than acceptable fabric capacity" to indicate reduced fabric capacity conditions.

items.synopsis: Traffic impact is observed due to rapid interface flapping on PTX12008 routers or devices equipped with JNP10K-LC1301 FPC or JNP10008-SF5 SIB modules
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX12008 platform or devices equipped with JNP10K-LC1301 FPC (Flexible PIC Concentrator) or JNP10008-SF5 SIB (Switch Interface Board) cards, a rapid (sub-second) interface flap triggers a timing issue that causes the evo-cda-bx process to hog CPU resources. These periods of high CPU utilization affect other processes and protocols, ultimately impacting traffic on the device.

items.synopsis: On Linux based platforms, kernel panic and crash observed during firmware download due to a device removal race condition
items.description: On Linux based Junos and Junos-Evo platforms, system might experience a kernel panic and unexpected restart if a firmware download is in progress when the associated device is removed, reset, or undergoes a line-card or PCIe card flap. This is a low-probability, timing-dependent issue that requires the firmware download and device-removal operations has to happen simultaneously.

items.category: Issues related to NTP issues on evo
items.synopsis: Nagios server not able to connect to ACX7024X
items.description: On EVO ACX platforms with VRF/loopback/vrrp when ntpd replies to client requests the NTP server responses uses incorrect source addresses instead of the destination address of the received packet, causing NTP client queries to fail or receive responses from unexpected source addresses.

items.synopsis: SRX400/SRX440 upgrade fails and enters a boot loop when using an empty USB drive to upgrade
items.description: On SRX400 and SRX440 platforms, when the upgrade is performed using an empty USB drive along with an incomplete/incorrect/inaccessible PXE (Preboot Execution Environment) configuration, the upgrade fails, and the device enters a reboot loop.

items.synopsis: SIB recovery failure results in prolonged traffic blackholing on PTX10003 platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX10003 platforms, a rare fabric fault on a SIB (Switch Interface Board) causes the SIB to stop forwarding traffic. A failure to recover the affected SIB results in repeated traffic blackholing and prolonged traffic disruption.

items.category: EVO L3 routing for BCM XGS Platforms
items.synopsis: On all Junos Evolved QFX platforms IPv6 static /56 routes stop forwarding traffic after route reprocessing triggered by topology changes
items.description: On all Junos Evolved QFX platforms, IPv6 traffic destined to networks reachable through affected IPv6 static /56 routes stops forwarding after topology changes such as reboots or link flaps cause route reprocessing. This results in loss of IPv6 connectivity for the affected prefixes.

items.synopsis: Physical interface creation failure was ignored resulting in system crash or traffic blackhole
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX Series routers, during physical interface deactivate/activate operations, failure to recreate a physical Interface Device (IFD) resulted in an inconsistent interface state. This issue caused a system crash leading to service disruption or traffic blackhole.

items.synopsis: Firewall logs always display ICMP type 0
items.description: On all MX platforms running MPC10E, MPC11E, MX10K-LC4802, and MX10K-LC9600 line cards, as well as Junos OS Evolved platforms, when a firewall filter term with the log action matches Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) traffic, firewall logs display ICMP packets as type 0, preventing administrators from identifying the actual ICMP type in logged traffic.

items.synopsis: Traffic flooding will occur when LAGs span both AE interface pools on Junos OS Evolved Platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, When Link Aggregation Groups (LAGs) were configured across different AE interface pools (ae0-ae1999 and ae2000+)sharing the same hardware trunk identifier. Under specific conditions, a Media Access Control (MAC) flush event on one LAG could inadvertently remove MAC entries for another LAG from hardware while retaining them in software, leading to traffic flooding and forwarding disruption.

items.synopsis: PTP synchronization failure after reboot when PTP is configured over an AE interface
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms with PTP (Precision Time Protocol) G.8275.1 profile configured over a LAG (Link Aggregation Group) interface, PTP will remain in the Acquiring state following a device reboot or RE (Routing Engine) switchover. This occurs because, after the reboot, an unexpected value is passed during PTP hardware programming. As a result, the hardware programming operation fails, preventing PTP from completing synchronization and transitioning out of the Acquiring state, resulting in PTP timing inaccuracies and impacting time-sensitive services.

items.synopsis: Multiple link flaps observed on all ACX7K platforms
items.description: On all ACX7K platforms, an internal ASIC interrupt was triggered in two different scenarios, in some cases the issue is seen without any change in the configuration and in some other cases the issue is seen when an egress sflow (sampled Flow) and egress mirror was enabled/attached to the same interface and committed. The triggered interrupt causes multiple interface flaps and temporary suspension of the ASIC programming resulting in transient disruption of forwarding operations and packet loss.

items.synopsis: MPC11 line card in SUBLC configuration within a GNF remain stuck in 'Present' state during online or offline operations
items.description: On Junos MX2010 and MX2020 platforms with MPC11 line cards in a Sub Line Card (SUBLC) configuration within a Guest Network Function (GNF), SUBLC become stuck in the "Present" state. This is triggered after 10 days of system uptime when periodic filesystem cleaning deletes the critical /tmp/clmd directory, and any direct or indirect attempts to bring SLCs offline/online will trigger the issue. This results in a localized line-card outage and traffic impact.

items.synopsis: The Routing Engine reboots unexpectedly and reports "MSMI error/hw misc"
items.description: On affected ACX7300 platforms, a hardware-related condition causes the Routing Engine to stop responding and reboot unexpectedly. When the issue occurs, the reboot reason is reported as "MSMI error/hw misc". Routing protocols and network services are interrupted while the Routing Engine restarts and recovers.

items.synopsis: The sensord generates a crash file and triggers an MPC10 line card restart on MX platforms
items.description: On MX platforms with MPC10 line cards, the sensord daemon generates a crash file due to a race condition associated with telemetry subscriptions to sensors such as cmerror, fabric, transceiver, and optics. The issue can occur with explicit telemetry sensor subscriptions or with subscriptions that are active by default and results in an MPC10 line card restart and service impact on the affected line card.

items.synopsis: Excessive xcvr config_mismatch DEBUG messages were generated in picd during periodic monitoring
items.description: On Junos EVO PTX Series platforms (PTX12008, PTX10001-36MR, and PTX10003-160C), when a transceiver (xcvr) configuration mismatch alarm was present, the picd periodic transceiver monitoring process generated repetitive DEBUG log messages. The issue was observed in environments containing transceivers reporting configuration mismatch alarms. During periodic monitoring, the same mismatch and alarm conditions were repeatedly logged, resulting in excessive growth of picd logs.

items.category: Transport daemon for Packet Optical applications
items.synopsis: Optical performance monitoring becomes unavailable on PTX platforms with high scale of coherent-ZR interfaces
items.description: On Junos Evolved PTX platforms, systems with approximately 240 or more interfaces configured on ports using coherent-ZR optics (such as 100ZR and 400ZR transceivers) experience a loss of optical performance monitoring functionality. As a result, optical performance monitoring data, alarms, and statistics are no longer available through management interfaces.

items.synopsis: ACX configuring RFC2544 unsupported commands ovlan-id and/or ivlan-id causes configd process to crash
items.description: On ACX Series Platforms committing an RFC2544 service that includes unsupported VLAN-related RFC2544 attributes ovlan-id or ivlan-id. When RFC2544 service monitoring was configured together with Circuit Cross Connect (CCC), VLAN-CCC interfaces, or Layer 2 Circuit (L2Circuit) services. After the triggering configuration is processed, configd repeatedly restarts, generates core files. ACX Series Platforms running Junos Evo software are affected. Impact low.

items.category: PTX10K Line Card specific interface PRs
items.synopsis: Incorrect optics module temperature readings can cause the optics to shut down
items.description: On MX platforms with MPC11, LC9600, LC4800, LC4802 Linecards, MX304 & MX301 and all Junos OS Evolved platforms, QSFP28 optics modules intermittently reports report false high temperature values leading to optics shutdown.

items.synopsis: EVO: RPC "get-power-usage-information" for cli "show chassis power" shows error wtih ODL response
items.description: RPC "get-power-usage-information" for cli "show chassis power" shows error wtih ODL response

items.synopsis: Incorrect allocated power values are returned via telemetry
items.description: Due to missing capdb change, telemetry incorrectly reports the allocated power values for RCB and fan tray.

items.synopsis: PTX10K power supply input failure SNMP traps do not include the affected input feed information
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX10K platforms with an AC3H power supply module (PSM) installed, when an input feed failure occurs, the generated Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) jnxPowerSupplyInputFailure trap does not include information identifying the affected input feed. This limits the ability of SNMP-based monitoring applications to accurately identify the failed power input feed from the trap notification alone. This issue does not affect production traffic forwarding or cause service interruption.

items.category: ZT/YTpfe bridging, learning, stp, oam, irb software
items.synopsis: Hamilton :: LC4800 :: Initial Sync values not streaming
items.description: Hamilton :: LC4800 :: Initial Sync values not streaming

items.synopsis: Traffic drop may occur on AFT platforms due to incorrect TPID programming during configuration
items.description: On MX platforms with line cards MPC10/MPC11/LC4800/LC9600 or MX304, MX301, the TPID(Tag Protocol Identifier) for the unicast encapsulation next hop to be incorrectly programmed as 0x0 if the output interface is RLT . As a result, packets may be dropped by the PFE with an "unknown family" exception, causing traffic impact.

items.category: Configuration mgmt, ffp, load-action, commit processing
items.synopsis: Netconf RPC commit fails due to commit warning received for unprotect operation, CLI commit completes with warning
items.description: In Netconf private edit configuration session, commit RPC fails when unprotect operation is performed.

items.synopsis: Persistent hwdre anomaly alarm after a hardware alarm condition is cleared on Junos OS Evolved platforms
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, a anomaly errors reported for application hwdre on node re0 can continue to be reported after an underlying hardware alarm condition has cleared because a stale alarm object is retained. For example, this can occur after a temperature threshold alarm is raised and subsequently cleared. This results in a false alarm indication but does not impact traffic forwarding, routing, hardware health, or services.
